scenario: A third one gets away — the market's card, and this race's habit
note: The alternative, and it has a strong recent record on this race rather than being a theoretical hedge — Valdelinares and Calar Alto both went to the escape, the second of them to a rider the boards had at #23. References are the canonical mountain-escape days (mountain 0.47-0.52 over rolling, winner groups of 1 to 4): Carapaz's TdF 2026 stage 18, Soler's Vuelta 2025 stage 14, Barre's Pologne 2026 stage 6, van der Poel's TdF 2026 stage 9, Narvaez's Giro 2026 stage 11. The conditional pool cuts the GC top 10 — everyone inside 11:06, through Berthet — which frees the market's whole card: Buitrago (18th), Widar (14th), Cristian Rodriguez (11th), Bisiaux (12th), Berrade (24th), Johannessen (25th), Paret-Peintre (43rd) and Fortunato (73rd). Note the cut deliberately keeps Omrzel OUT of the free pool: he won from the break at Calar Alto but that win moved him to 6th on GC at +4:59, so he is now a rider the leaders have to watch rather than one they will let go — which is also why a repeat by him would score gc_day rather than res_2.
